title: The Ant Who Needed a Transplant
author: Bill Wall
mlbSummary: A young ant family learns what it means when their father needs a heart transplant, including waiting, worry, receiving a donor heart, and thinking about the donor family. The story uses a child-friendly animal family to introduce a difficult transplant experience.
notes: Amazon product verified. Secular medical story with no identified religious theme.

title: Nephrology for Kids
author: Brandon Pham and Betty Nguyen
mlbSummary: A physician-written introduction to the kidneys and renal system that explains kidney anatomy, how kidneys filter blood, kidney disease, and common tests in straightforward language for young readers.
notes: Amazon product constructed from verified ISBN-10 and cross-checked against publisher and hospital resource listings. No religious theme identified.

title: The Great Katie Kate Explains Epilepsy
author: M. Maitland DeLand
mlbSummary: Jimmy worries after being diagnosed with epilepsy, and the superhero Great Katie Kate helps him and other children learn about seizures, triggers, treatment, and questions they may have about living with epilepsy.
notes: Amazon product link verified directly through publisher. No religious theme identified.

title: My Life Beyond Sickle Cell Disease
author: Hey Gee and Golden Ella
audience: Children with Sickle Cell Disease & Families
mlbSummary: A graphic nonfiction Mayo Clinic patient story about a young athlete learning to manage sickle cell disease with support from her healthcare team and family while continuing to pursue goals on and off the track.
notes: Amazon product constructed from verified ISBN-10. Age range, publisher, and medical focus verified. No religious theme identified.

title: Life's a Polyp with Zeke and Katie
author: Jenny Jones
mlbSummary: An age-appropriate introduction to familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) that helps children understand the condition, what they may experience, and ways to cope with a rare inherited medical diagnosis.
notes: Amazon product verified from author/foundation media listing. Age range and ISBN verified through publisher. No religious theme identified.

title: Your Transplant Adventure! A Kid's Guide to Organ Transplant
author: Matt Butler and Tanya Smith
mlbSummary: Created by transplant social workers, this question-and-answer picture guide walks children through common parts of solid-organ transplantation, including surgery, stitches and scars, hospital care, recovery, and worries children may have before or after transplant.
notes: Direct Amazon product link supplied by Transplant Families. Developed at the University of Michigan Transplant Center. No religious theme identified.

title: Howl Learns About Kidneys and Dialysis
author: Brenda E. Cortez
mlbSummary: Howl visits his grandfather during dialysis and learns in simple language about kidney disease, dialysis treatment, the kidney waiting list, and the search for a donor. The story introduces dialysis equipment and routines without losing the family perspective.
notes: ISBN verified by the American Association of Kidney Patients and age guidance verified by the publisher. Amazon product uses the ISBN-10/ASIN. No religious theme identified.

title: Howl Loves His New Liver
author: Brenda E. Cortez
mlbSummary: Howl needs a liver transplant and the story follows his experience waiting on the transplant list while his family also looks for a living donor. It gives young children a concrete way to talk about liver transplantation, organ donation, and receiving a new organ.
notes: Exact ISBN and Amazon listing cross-checked through pediatric transplant resources and booksellers. No religious theme identified.
sourceCollections: Howl the Owl organ donation series

title: A Transplant for Ivy
author: Emilie Burgess, LMSW
mlbSummary: Ivy and her mother move through the experience of waiting for an organ transplant and receiving the call to come to the hospital. The story is designed to reassure children that other kids also go through transplant and that a donated organ can be a life-changing gift.
notes: Amazon KDP title with ASIN cross-checked through bibliographic listings. No religious theme identified in available descriptions.

title: Extraordinary! A Book for Children with Rare Diseases
author: Evren Ayik and Kara Ayik
mlbSummary: Written by a mother and son drawing on the son's experience with an ultra-rare genetic disease, this illustrated book helps children explore identity, inclusion, self-concept, and the challenges and strengths that can come with living with a rare diagnosis.
notes: ISBN and Amazon availability verified through the authors' site, Google Books, and rare-disease resource lists. The story focuses on identity, inclusion, and rare disease; no religious theme identified.

title: I Am Rare: Discovering What Makes Us Shine
author: Melissa White Boyer
audience: Children with Rare Genetic Conditions & Families
mlbSummary: A lyrical picture book narrated by a child with a rare genetic condition that introduces genes and mutations while exploring identity, belonging, confidence, and the idea that being rare means being uncommon rather than being wrong.
notes: Published August 2026. Exact Amazon ASIN cross-checked against bibliographic listings, author materials, and independent reviews. No religious theme identified.

title: The Tale of the Cell
author: Georgene' Glass
audience: Young Children with Sickle Cell Disease & Families
mlbSummary: Gia's story introduces young readers to sickle cell disease, including the pain and challenges it can cause, how sickle cell trait can be inherited, and the role of family and a healthcare support team. The book is designed both for children living with sickle cell and for peers learning about the condition.
notes: Paperback ISBN, age guidance, author, illustrator, and Amazon availability cross-checked through the foundation, booksellers, media coverage, and independent review. No religious theme identified.
